text:
erin: Quick catch from a customer call — their infra team expects to plug a credential sidecar (OIDC -> token file) but our SDKs don't expose a small "credential provider" hook. They end up restarting services on every rotation.

paul: ouch. which SDKs?

erin: python sampleapp + node microservice. node has an internal opt-in watcher but python and the CLI are read-once at init.

nitya: parity gap. Proposal: standardize a tiny provider interface across SDKs: `get_token()` returns token+expiry, `on_refresh(cb)` optional. Default providers: env, file(path), exec(cmd). Add a `watch=true` option for file provider.

paul: love it. for services we should recommend file + atomic swap by default. docs should show `mv new ~/.config/redwood/token && rw auth reload` example.

erin: also: precedence doc is missing. suggest we make it explicit: REDWOOD_API_KEY (env) > REDWOOD_TOKEN_FILE env (path) > ~/.config/redwood/token > cached runtime token > key-embedded defaults. Put that in sampleapp README and CLI help.

ci-bot: created issue RBW-6022 (labels: devex, sdk, onboarding)

nitya: runtime behavior: lazy-read with small TTL (3s) for ordinary requests, but for long-lived streams add in-stream reauth: on 401/403, call provider.get_token() once and attempt a single resume. If still rejected, surface fatal error. This avoids expensive watchers in all apps.

paul: add CLI helpers: `rw auth reload` (signals parent process or calls provider reload) and `rw auth provider add --type file --path /var/run/redwood/token --watch` to register provider config in `~/.config/redwood/providers.json`. Also `rw auth status` should print effective sources and precedence so devs know what to rotate.

erin: telemetry: emit `auth.provider.refresh` and `auth.reauth_attempt` events with lightweight metadata (provider type, success/fail). Support can use those to correlate rotation pain.

keith: server-side nicety: when we revoke keys, can we return `X-Reauth-Required: 1` or `Retry-After: 2` headers so clients can differentiate forced revocation vs expiry? Also `X-Allowed-Projects` on 403 would help CLI preflight UX.

paul: preflight idea: before any large upload or multi-chunk stream, do a small scope-check call that validates key/project combos and fails fast with a clear error listing allowed scopes. That prevents partial uploads then 403s.

erin: tests: unit test for provider interface, integration test simulating atomic token swap + stream resume, CLI test for `rw auth reload`. Docs: add a short "Rotating tokens for services" section with systemd and k8s examples (secret update + rolling restart or provider file atomic swap + `rw auth reload`).

nitya: i'll draft the provider interface spec and a minimal python adapter (file watch optional). paul can add CLI helpers + docs. I'll also add env-var precedence text to SDK READMEs.

paul: sounds good. tagging @eng-runtime for header suggestions. thanks everyone — this should cut a lot of onboarding friction. :thumbsup:
